minutes.headline: Committee leans toward renovating Ritter and Town Hall, not building new, targeting an eight-figure cost
minutes.summary: The Building Design Committee reviewed a member's space-allocation spreadsheet (165 sq ft per employee) for Ritter and Town Hall, compared it line by line against the earlier Taylor and Burns study, and debated whether Ritter is even the right building to renovate. No formal decision was voted on the building question; the committee agreed to aim for a combined project in the "eight figures" and to set up a subcommittee meeting before talking to town employees about their space needs.

votes.motion: Approve the meeting minutes of November 17th, 2020 (as heard)

budget_items.what_was_said: A member proposed allocating office space using an industry-standard square-footage-per-person figure, illustrated with the assessor's office as an example.
The presenter totaled the proposed public-facing space and the private/non-public space separately across all departments.
The presenter described the size of the current 1963/1965 addition to Ritter as measured from a rough architectural sketch.
Doubling the existing addition footprint (up or down) was proposed as enough space to house the public-facing functions.
The original Ritter building footprint was estimated per level and in total, proposed to hold the private/non-public functions.

budget_items.topic: Cost of filling in corridor gap
budget_items.what_was_said: Filling the gap between the addition and the original building to make a full rectangle was estimated to add cost per level and overall.
A back-of-napkin cost estimate for a new addition was given using the Taylor and Burns per-square-foot construction rate.
An additional allowance was added for careful, non-destructive demolition of the 1963/65 addition to protect the original Ritter building.

budget_items.topic: Rehab cost and total project estimate
budget_items.what_was_said: Using a rehab rate drawn from the Taylor and Burns study, the presenter totaled demolition, new construction and rehab into one project figure.
The chair compared the Taylor and Burns square footage for the treasurer and tax collector functions against the newer proposal.
Town clerk space including the vault and registry of voters was compared between the two studies.
Assessor's office square footage was compared between the Taylor and Burns figures and the new proposal.
Building department space, including a waiting room and record storage, was compared, with a question raised about whether an assistant building inspector position exists.
Town manager space was compared between the two studies, with the newer proposal allocating less.
The presenter proposed reducing total allocated space by a fifth, splitting it between employee work space and shared space like restrooms, hallways and conference rooms.

A member framed the town's likely capacity for debt-excluded capital projects over the next decade, citing interest in Marshall Park, Turkey Hill, and admin facilities but resistance to a high price tag for the latter.

The chair stated a personal goal of keeping the combined Town Hall and Ritter project cost in the eight-figure range to improve chances of town-meeting approval, contrasting it with a much larger figure he believes would not pass.

decisions.decision: The committee agreed on two guiding goals: find a workable plan for the town buildings that would be vacated, and keep the combined project fiscally responsible (around eight figures).
Subcommittee (Laura, Matt, Tony, with Greg Roy as an alternate to avoid a quorum issue) will meet at 1:00 pm on Tuesday the 10th, location to be the Ritter conference room if available.
The full committee's next meeting was set for March 2nd.

The chair stated the committee should treat renovating Ritter and Town Hall (rather than building new) as settled given the committee's charter, though at least one member said he remained unconvinced Ritter is the right building.

what_happened.line: The chair said the committee's charter already settles renovating Ritter and Town Hall rather than building new, though one member said he remains unconvinced Ritter is the right building.
With no formal vote, the committee set two goals: keep the combined project in the eight figures and find a plan for the buildings it would vacate.
A subcommittee was scheduled to meet before the committee talks to town employees about their space needs.
The next full committee meeting was set for March 2.
A member's space-allocation spreadsheet, built on a square-footage-per-employee standard, was compared department by department against the earlier Taylor and Burns study.

why_it_matters: This concerns a likely debt-excluded capital project for Ritter and Town Hall, which would appear as a separate line on a future tax bill rather than inside the town's operating budget.
The committee is steering toward renovation over new construction before any formal vote or public comment on that choice has occurred.
Town employees whose departments were sized in the spreadsheet have not yet been consulted on their space needs.
